products.title: CONUS Weather Radar Base Reflectivity
products.description: Weather radar base reflectivity mosaics of CONUS radar data from Weather Surveillance Radar 1988 Doppler (WSR-88D) sites operated by NWS and DOD and also from Terminal Doppler Weather Radars at major airports. The colors on the map represent the strength of the energy reflected back towards the radar measured in dBZ. The horizontal resolution is  1km (0.62 mi). The mosaics are updated approximately every 4 minutes. Data source: NWS & OAR Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor (MRMS) System.
products.coverageMessage: Radar coverage is not verified; blank areas may have no return or missing data.

legend.explanation: Radar reflectivity, not rainfall depth or certainty of rain at the surface.

products.title: GOES East & West Satellite Longwave Imagery
products.description: NOAA/NASA Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES) Longwave Infrared Band 14 (11.2 μm), has a 5 min update frequency and a 2 km spatial resolution. Data from the 11.2 μm channel is used in many Baseline Products, such as Fire Detection, Volcanic Ash Detection, Derived Motion Wind Vectors, Legacy Atmospheric Profiles including Precipitable Water, Cloud Top Properties, Aerosol Detection and Land Surface Temperature. This composite longwave imagery contains GOES-19 (East) and GOES-18 (West) from GOES Advanced Baseline Imager (ABI) Level 1b (L1b), L1b products are calibrated and, where applicable, geographically corrected.

legend.explanation: Infrared cloud/surface patterns. Provider legend is illustrative, not a validated Celsius scale or surface air temperature.

products.title: Global Satellite Longwave Imagery
products.description: The NOAA/NESDIS Global Mosaic of Geostationary Satellite Imagery (GMGSI) longwave, thermal infrared band (~12.0 μm), has an hourly update frequency, approximately 3 km spatial resolution, the data latency is two to three hours and depicts cloud cover and land/sea temperature patterns. The channel is used in many baseline products, such as Fire Detection, Volcanic Ash Detection, and Derived Motion Wind Vector.
